trung.quote: Over the years, I've regularly reached out to TTC-Infotech whenever an IT issue came up. Every single time, the problem was resolved quickly and the engineers were friendly and professional. It made me realize: if the computer system breaks down and I can't find the cause, just call TTC-Infotech right away — because I know that if I don't, I'm only wasting time while the problem stays unsolved. As soon as I want it fixed, I call the help desk and it gets handled immediately. You guys do an awesome job.

toan.quote: We'd like to thank the TTC-Infotech team for the impeccable service they've provided us. There's simply no comparison between before and after working together. Previously, every power outage or system failure cost us hours of lost productivity. We went through nearly six different IT providers, all slow to respond, forcing us to manage IT on our own. If our server went down in the middle of the night, someone from the company had to come in and manually reboot it — our day-to-day infrastructure was a mess that pulled focus away from our core business. With the TTC-Infotech team, our fears about IT failures were eased thanks to their expertise, network improvements, proactive monitoring, and remote remediation capabilities. Whenever we need support, we get it through their 24/7 operations center, and we can always count on the team to answer our calls at any time of day. Now that disruptions are minimal, our staff can focus on their daily work. Thank you TTC-Infotech for the fast, reliable service — we look forward to continued success together!

dung.quote: We want to thank TTC-Infotech for becoming a true extension of our organization. With your support, our systems were quickly back up and running, and downtime dropped significantly thanks to the team's efficiency. As you know, our fast-growing needs and constantly evolving technology requirements demand that our business stays cutting-edge with minimal downtime. In our past experience with another IT provider, we kept running into power, performance, and server issues that were never fully resolved — finding a new managed IT partner became inevitable. When our server crashed, TTC-Infotech was fortunately able to step in immediately to handle the emergency. Choosing TTC-Infotech, we knew we'd made the right call — we no longer have to monitor our own servers and network ourselves, and can instead rely on an entire team of experts to keep up with the complex technology upgrades our industry demands. I'd happily recommend TTC-Infotech to any small, medium, or large business looking for fast service and a reliable team of experts with the best solutions for their industry.

minh.quote: Working with TTC-Infotech has been a wonderful experience. Thanks to the consistent, reliable response from their expert team, our office now operates far more efficiently. Having worked with a different IT provider before and struggled with slow service and response times, we needed a partner we could truly count on — one that could keep up with our ever-changing technology needs and implement a proactive IT plan we could rely on for the future. During a server crash with our former provider, we lost critical data. TTC-Infotech's team of professionals worked diligently to put in place a proper backup and disaster recovery plan and fixed the data-sync issues they uncovered along the way. TTC-Infotech lets us focus on what we do best — building our clients' brands. Thanks to their team, we no longer have to worry about maintaining our network, because we can fully trust TTC-Infotech to proactively monitor it for us.

comparison.heading: VMware vs. Proxmox VE
comparison.intro: VMware (now part of Broadcom) and Proxmox VE are two leading enterprise virtualization platforms, but they follow completely opposite design philosophies and business models. VMware focuses on standardization and high reliability for large enterprises, while Proxmox VE is a feature-rich, flexible open-source platform that keeps costs low.

rows.label: Nature / Architecture
rows.col2: Type-1 hypervisor based on Linux (Debian) + KVM + LXC

rows.label: Licensing model
rows.col1: Commercial (subscription required since the Broadcom acquisition)
rows.col2: Open source (AGPLv3), fully featured for free; pay only for a support plan

rows.label: Container virtualization
rows.col2: Built-in LXC (Linux Containers), lightweight and high-performance

rows.label: Centralized management
rows.col1: Requires a separately installed vCenter Server (extra resources and cost)
rows.col2: Built-in Web UI on every node, cluster forms automatically when nodes are joined

rows.label: Storage
rows.col1: VMFS, NFS, iSCSI, vSAN (requires a premium license)
rows.col2: ZFS, Ceph (built-in SDS), LVM, NFS, iSCSI, Directory

rows.label: Backup and recovery
rows.col1: Relies on third parties (Veeam, Commvault, Nakivo...)
rows.col2: Built-in VZDump, or paired with Proxmox Backup Server (PBS)

rows.label: Ecosystem and support
rows.col1: Very large, industry standard, 24/7 enterprise support
rows.col2: Strong community, official support through Enterprise Subscription

details.title: Core architecture and management
details.col1: ESXi uses its own VMkernel. Managing one or more ESXi clusters requires vCenter Server — a dedicated virtual server that consumes resources. If vCenter fails, centralized management is interrupted even though the virtual machines keep running.
details.col2: Built on Debian Linux with a multi-master architecture: you can open the Web GUI of any node in the cluster to manage the entire system. Beyond KVM for hardware virtualization, Proxmox natively supports LXC, letting you run hundreds of ultra-light containers at almost zero CPU/RAM overhead.

details.title: Cost and licensing model
details.col1: Since the Broadcom acquisition, VMware has stopped selling perpetual licenses and moved to recurring subscription bundles (VCF or VVF) priced by the number of CPU cores (minimum 16 cores per socket), sharply raising total cost of ownership (TCO).
details.col2: Download and use 100% of the features at no cost. Proxmox's paid subscription only applies when a business needs access to the thoroughly tested official update repository (Enterprise Repository) and direct technical support from the vendor (priced per CPU socket per year, significantly cheaper than VMware).

details.title: Storage and backup ecosystem
details.col1: Uses vSAN to turn local disks into shared SAN storage, but requires strictly HCL-compliant hardware and an expensive license. For backup, VMware relies on the third-party ecosystem such as Veeam Backup & Replication — the industry benchmark for speed and features.
details.col2: Built-in Ceph and ZFS let you build hyper-converged infrastructure (HCI) entirely in software with no extra licensing cost. For backup, Proxmox developed its own Proxmox Backup Server (PBS) — with block-level data deduplication, incremental backup, and highly effective client-side encryption.

guidance.title: Choose VMware when
items: The infrastructure runs mission-critical business applications for a large enterprise.
The system is already standardized on the VMware HCL.
Operations depend closely on tools such as Veeam and vRealize (VMware Aria).
The IT budget is generous.

guidance.title: Choose Proxmox when
items: The business wants to optimize licensing cost.
The infrastructure is small to medium-sized (SMB).
The data center wants to move away from dependence on Broadcom.
The environment needs flexibility between both virtual machines (VMs) and containers.
